name: Mahamat Déby
milestone_by_age_26: Promoted to brigadier general in May 2009 at age 25 and shared command of Chadian forces during the Battle of Am Dam, where the army defeated UFR rebels.
early_history_summary: Born to Idriss Déby, then commander-in-chief of the Chadian Ground Forces and later president of Chad, Mahamat was sent to military training in France and Chad. He first saw combat in April 2006 at age 22 when rebels attacked the capital, and rose rapidly through the ranks of the presidential guard and security services.
family_context_summary: Son of Idriss Déby, who was commander-in-chief of the Chadian Ground Forces at the time of Mahamat's birth and became president of Chad in 1990, ruling for over 30 years.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a military commander and then president; Mahamat was embedded in the Chadian military command structure from the start of his career, with rapid promotions reflecting his family position.
primary_early_advantage_tags: presidential family, military dynasty, nepotism, combat exposure, elite security forces
evidence_summary: Mahamat Déby is the son of Chad's long-ruling president Idriss Déby, which gave him direct access to the military command structure from a young age. He was trained at military schools in Chad and France, joined the presidential guard, and saw combat at 22. By 25, he was promoted to brigadier general and shared command at the Battle of Am Dam. His rapid rise is inseparable from his father's position as head of state and military commander.
starting_point: Born in N'Djamena, Chad in 1984 as the son of Idriss Déby, then commander-in-chief of the Chadian Ground Forces who would become president in 1990.
current_position: President of Chad since May 2024, having served as de facto head of state and leader of the Transitional Military Council since April 2021; holds rank of Marshal.

trajectory.event: First combat experience defending the capital N'Djamena during a rebel attack.
Promoted to brigadier general and shared command of Chadian forces at the Battle of Am Dam, defeating UFR rebels.
Appointed director of the DGSSIE, the presidential guard and special forces organization.
Became de facto head of state and president of the Transitional Military Council after his father was killed in combat.
Won the presidential election with 61% of the vote and was sworn in as president of Chad on 23 May 2024.

name: Vladimír Dzurilla
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze medal at the 1964 Innsbruck Olympics at age 22, and Olympic silver at the 1968 Grenoble Olympics at age 26, as goaltender for Czechoslovakia.
early_history_summary: Born in Bratislava, Dzurilla was discovered playing street hockey and joined Slovan Bratislava in exchange for 150 pucks and 50 hockey sticks. He made his top-league debut at age 17 in November 1959 and quickly became the team's starting goaltender, rising to the Czechoslovak national team by the early 1960s.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Dzurilla worked as a refrigerator repairman by profession alongside his hockey career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Czechoslovak hockey system, Slovan Bratislava, national team, early debut, goaltending talent
evidence_summary: Dzurilla was discovered playing street hockey in Bratislava and joined Slovan Bratislava at a young age, making his top-league debut at 17 in 1959. He rose through the Czechoslovak hockey pipeline to become the national team goaltender, winning Olympic bronze in 1964 and silver in 1968. No family background or financial advantages are documented; his career appears driven by natural talent and the Czechoslovak sports system.
starting_point: Born in Bratislava, Slovakia in 1942; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died in 1995 at age 52 in Düsseldorf, Germany from a heart attack; final role was as a goaltender in the German league after retiring from Czechoslovak hockey.

trajectory.event: Made his top-league debut for Slovan Bratislava, stepping in for an injured goaltender.
Won Olympic bronze medal at the Innsbruck Olympics as goaltender for Czechoslovakia.
Won Olympic silver medal at the Grenoble Olympics as goaltender for Czechoslovakia.
Famously stopped 29 shots in a 1-0 win over Canada at the 1976 Canada Cup.
Retired from professional hockey after four seasons in the German league.
Died of a heart attack at his home in Düsseldorf, Germany.

name: Murat Karayılan
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) in 1978-1979 and was an active militant organizer in southeastern Turkey by age 26, before fleeing to Syria after the 1980 Turkish coup.
early_history_summary: Born in Birecik, Şanlıurfa, Karayılan finished vocational college in machinery and joined the PKK in 1979 at age 25. He was active in organizing Kurdish resistance in his native province until the 1980 Turkish coup forced him to flee to Syria.
family_context_summary: Born in Birecik, Şanlıurfa province in southeastern Turkey, a predominantly Kurdish region. Family financial background not documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kurdish minority, political repression, Öcalan mentorship, guerrilla organizing
evidence_summary: Karayılan grew up in a Kurdish region of southeastern Turkey and joined the newly formed PKK at age 25, becoming one of its co-founders. His early trajectory was shaped by Kurdish political marginalization and the radical leftist milieu of 1970s Turkey. He was mentored by Abdullah Öcalan and worked alongside a small founding cadre before fleeing to Syria after the 1980 coup. No family advantages are documented.
starting_point: Born in 1954 in Birecik, Şanlıurfa, a predominantly Kurdish town in southeastern Turkey; family background not documented.
current_position: Commander-in-chief of the PKK's armed wing (People's Defence Forces) since 2014; one of the most senior leaders of the PKK, wanted by Turkey and the United States.

trajectory.event: Joined the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) as one of its co-founders and began organizing in Şanlıurfa province.
Fled to Syria after the 1980 Turkish military coup to continue PKK operations from exile.
Became acting leader of the PKK after Abdullah Öcalan was captured by Turkish intelligence.
Left the PKK political leader position and was assigned as commander-in-chief of the PKK's armed wing.

name: Koen Lenaerts
milestone_by_age_26: No material professional milestone by age 26; had completed a Harvard LLM (1978) and MPA (1979) but had not yet obtained his PhD (1982), begun his professorship (1983), or been appointed to any judicial position.
early_history_summary: Lenaerts studied law at the Université de Namur and KU Leuven, graduating summa cum laude, then earned an LLM and MPA from Harvard on a Fulbright scholarship. By age 26 he was still completing his academic training, with his PhD and professional career still ahead.
evidence_summary: Lenaerts had an elite academic trajectory, attending KU Leuven and Harvard Law School, but had not achieved a material professional milestone by age 26. His PhD, professorship, and judicial appointments all came later.

name: Michael Gambon
milestone_by_age_26: Hired as one of the original members of Laurence Olivier's National Theatre Company in 1963 at age 23, after making his professional stage debut at Dublin's Gate Theatre in 1962.
early_history_summary: Born in Dublin to a seamstress mother and engineering operative father, Gambon left school at 15 and trained as a toolmaker at Vickers-Armstrongs. At 24, he fabricated a CV to get hired at Dublin's Gate Theatre, then auditioned for Olivier's new National Theatre Company and was selected alongside Derek Jacobi and Robert Stephens.
family_context_summary: Born in Cabra, Dublin to a seamstress mother and an engineering operative father who moved the family to London when Gambon was six. Working-class background; left school at 15 with no qualifications.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to acting or the arts. Father was an engineering operative; mother was a seamstress.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Olivier mentorship, National Theatre, Gate Theatre, working-class background, ensemble peers
evidence_summary: Gambon came from a working-class Dublin-London family with no theatre connections. He left school at 15 for a toolmaking apprenticeship, then talked his way into Dublin's Gate Theatre with a fabricated CV at age 24. Within a year, he auditioned for Laurence Olivier's newly formed National Theatre Company and was hired as one of its original members, alongside future stars like Derek Jacobi. Olivier served as a direct mentor and gave him his film debut in Othello (1965).
starting_point: Born in Cabra, Dublin in 1940 to a seamstress mother and engineering operative father; family moved to London when he was six, raised working-class.
current_position: Died on 27 September 2023 at age 82 in Witham, Essex, England; final roles included Harry Potter's Dumbledore (2004-2011) and various television projects through 2019.

trajectory.event: Made professional stage debut at Dublin's Gate Theatre in Othello after fabricating his CV.
Hired by Laurence Olivier as an original member of the National Theatre Company.
Made film debut in Olivier's Othello alongside Maggie Smith and Derek Jacobi.
Won first BAFTA TV Award for Best Actor for The Singing Detective.
Knighted by Queen Elizabeth II for services to drama.
Began role as Albus Dumbledore in the Harry Potter film series, gaining worldwide recognition.
Died on 27 September 2023 in Witham, Essex.

name: Marcelo Ríos
milestone_by_age_26: Finished as the world's No. 1 junior player in 1993 winning the US Open junior title at age 17; reached ATP world No. 1 in March 1998 at age 23, becoming the first Latin American to hold the top ranking.
early_history_summary: Ríos began playing tennis at age 11 at the Sport Francés golf club in Vitacura, adjacent to his house. He won the junior US Open in 1993 without dropping a set, turned professional in 1994, and won his first ATP title in 1995 at age 19. He reached world No. 1 in 1998 after winning the Miami Masters against Andre Agassi.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Santiago, Chile with a tennis club adjacent to his house. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early tennis start, junior No. 1, ATP tour, coaching, left-handed talent
evidence_summary: Ríos started playing tennis at 11 at a club next to his home in Santiago and rose to become the world's No. 1 junior player by 17, winning the US Open junior title. He turned professional at 19 and reached ATP world No. 1 at 23, the first Latin American to do so. No significant family advantages are documented; his trajectory was driven by early specialization, natural talent, and professional coaching.
starting_point: Born in Santiago, Chile in 1975; grew up with a tennis club adjacent to his house in Vitacura. Family financial background not documented.
current_position: Retired from professional tennis in 2004 due to chronic back injuries; resides in Santiago, Chile. Career prize money of approximately US$9.7 million.

trajectory.event: Finished as world No. 1 junior player, winning the US Open junior singles title without dropping a set.
Won his first ATP tournament title in Bologna and broke into the world's top 50.
Became ATP world No. 1 in singles, the first Latin American to hold the top ranking, after winning the Miami Masters.
Retired from professional tennis due to persistent back injuries.

name: Harold Pinter
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone as a playwright by age 26; his first play 'The Room' was produced in 1957 when he was 27. Before that, he was a working repertory actor under the stage name David Baron, with no notable creative breakthrough.
early_history_summary: Pinter attended RADA briefly, then worked as a professional actor in repertory theatre from 1951 to 1959 under the stage name David Baron, playing over 20 roles. He published poetry from 1947 but did not produce his first play until 1957 at age 27.
family_context_summary: Born in Hackney, east London, the only child of a ladies' tailor father and a housewife mother. Described as a solid, red-brick, three-storey villa. Working-class Jewish family of Eastern European descent.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connection to theatre or literature. Father was a ladies' tailor.
evidence_summary: Pinter was a professional repertory actor from 1951 to 1959 but did not produce his first play until 1957 at age 27, just after the age 26 cutoff. His Nobel Prize, major plays, and screenwriting career all came well after age 26. No material creative milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Veljo Tormis
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; had completed studies at the Moscow Conservatory (1951-1956) and started a teaching position at the Tallinn Music School, but his first notable compositions (Kihnu pulmalaulud, Overture No. 2) came in 1959 at age 29.
early_history_summary: Tormis began formal musical education in 1943 at the Tallinn Music School, entered the Tallinn Conservatory in 1949, and continued at the Moscow Conservatory from 1951 to 1956. His father was a choral director and organist, giving him early exposure to music. By 26 he was a trained composer and teacher but had not yet produced notable works.
family_context_summary: Born in Kuusalu, Estonia in 1930. His father was a choral director, organist, and music teacher, providing early immersion in choral music.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a choral director, organist, and music teacher, which gave Tormis direct early exposure to choral music and organ timbres that shaped his later style.
evidence_summary: Tormis had a strong musical upbringing through his father, a choral director and organist, and completed elite training at the Moscow Conservatory by age 26. However, his first notable compositions did not appear until 1959 when he was 29. No material creative milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Aribert Reimann
milestone_by_age_26: His first stage work, the ballet 'Stoffreste' to a libretto by Günter Grass, premiered at the Städtische Bühnen in Essen on 12 February 1959 when Reimann was 23 years old.
early_history_summary: Born in Berlin to a choirmaster father and oratorio singer mother, Reimann composed his first lieder at age 10. He studied composition at the Musikhochschule Berlin with Boris Blacher and worked as a répétiteur at the Städtische Oper. His first concerts as pianist and accompanist were in 1957, followed by the ballet premiere in 1959.
family_context_summary: Born in Berlin in 1936 to a musical family. His father Wolfgang Reimann was choirmaster at Berlin Cathedral, and his mother was an oratorio singer and voice teacher.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a choirmaster at Berlin Cathedral and mother was a professional oratorio singer and voice teacher, providing direct immersion in classical music and opera from birth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: musical family, Berlin Cathedral choir, opera house immersion, Boris Blacher, Günter Grass collaboration
evidence_summary: Reimann grew up in a deeply musical household in Berlin: his father was choirmaster at Berlin Cathedral and his mother an oratorio singer and voice teacher. He composed his first lieder at age 10, studied composition with Boris Blacher at the Musikhochschule Berlin, and worked as a répétiteur at the Städtische Oper. His ballet Stoffreste, to a libretto by Günter Grass, premiered at the Essen opera house in February 1959 when he was just 23. This family-domain apprenticeship and early institutional access were central to his precocious career.
starting_point: Born in Berlin in 1936 to a musical family; father was choirmaster at Berlin Cathedral and mother was an oratorio singer and voice teacher.
current_position: Died on 13 March 2024 at age 88 in Berlin; was a renowned composer and professor, best known for his opera Lear (1978) and receiving the Ernst von Siemens Music Prize in 2011.

trajectory.event: Gave his first concerts as pianist and lied accompanist while studying at the Musikhochschule Berlin.
Ballet Stoffreste, to a libretto by Günter Grass, premiered at the Städtische Bühnen in Essen.
First opera Ein Traumspiel premiered at the Opernhaus Kiel.
Opera Lear premiered at the Bavarian State Opera with Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau in the title role, becoming a lasting success.
Awarded the Ernst von Siemens Music Prize for his life's work.
Died on 13 March 2024 in Berlin.

name: Ettore Scola
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; entered the film industry as a screenwriter in 1953 at age 22, but his first notable screenplay (Il Sorpasso, 1962) came at 31 and his first directed film in 1964 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Scola was born in Trevico, Avellino, and became a ghostwriter at age 15. He entered the film industry as a screenwriter in 1953, but his breakthrough work came nearly a decade later with Il Sorpasso (1962) and his directorial debut in 1964.
family_context_summary: Born in Trevico, Avellino, Campania, Italy. Family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace.
evidence_summary: Scola entered the film industry as a screenwriter in 1953 at age 22, but his first notable screenplay (Il Sorpasso) did not come until 1962 when he was 31, and his directorial debut was in 1964 at age 33. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Marian Drăgulescu
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold on floor exercise and vault at the 2001 World Championships at age 20, adding to European Championship golds in 2000 and multiple World and European titles by age 26, including 8 World Championship golds.
early_history_summary: Drăgulescu started gymnastics as a boy in Bucharest, initially reluctant but eventually committed. His junior debut came at the 1998 European Championships where he won four medals. As a senior, he won his first World Championship golds in 2001 at age 20 and dominated vault and floor throughout the 2000s.
family_context_summary: Born in Bucharest, Romania in 1980. Family financial background not documented. Father was involved in his early sports decisions but details are limited.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond father's involvement in redirecting him back to gymnastics.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Romanian gymnastics system, CSA Steaua, junior European champion, vault specialist, eponymous skill
evidence_summary: Drăgulescu grew up in Bucharest and entered the Romanian gymnastics pipeline, one of the world's most elite systems. He won four medals at the 1998 European Junior Championships and his first World Championship golds at age 20 in 2001. His eponymous vault (handspring double front with half turn) is named after him in the Code of Points. No significant family advantages are documented; his trajectory was driven by the Romanian gymnastics system and natural talent.
starting_point: Born in Bucharest, Romania in 1980; family financial background not documented. Entered gymnastics as a young boy, initially reluctant.
current_position: Retired from competitive gymnastics after the 2021 Tokyo Olympics where he became the first artistic gymnast to represent Romania at five Olympic editions; works as a gymnastics coach. Most decorated male Romanian gymnast at World Championships with 8 gold medals.

trajectory.event: Won four medals at the European Junior Championships in St. Petersburg, including gold on pommel horse.
Won gold on floor exercise and vault at the World Championships in Ghent.
Won four gold medals at the European Championships and Olympic bronze in team and vault, silver in floor at the Athens Olympics.
Won gold on both floor and vault at the World Championships in Aarhus.
Won gold on floor and vault at the World Championships in London after coming out of retirement.
Became the first artistic gymnast to represent Romania at five Olympic Games at the Tokyo Olympics.

name: Christian Lacroix
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; was still a student of art history and museum studies at the Sorbonne and École du Louvre, aspiring to be a museum curator. His fashion career began at Jean Patou in 1985 and his own house launched in 1987.
early_history_summary: Lacroix was born in Arles, France, and studied art history at the University of Montpellier, then at the Sorbonne and École du Louvre in Paris. He married in 1974 and was working on a dissertation on dress in French 18th-century painting, aspiring to be a museum curator. He did not enter fashion until 1985.
family_context_summary: Born in Arles, Bouches-du-Rhône in southern France. Family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace and early interest in sketching historical costumes.
evidence_summary: Lacroix was still a university student studying art history and museum studies at age 26, aspiring to become a museum curator. He did not enter the fashion industry until 1985 at age 34, when he joined Jean Patou. His eponymous fashion house launched in 1987. No material milestone in fashion or any field by age 26 is documented.
